import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1072

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1072](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1072)
-/

open Nat Filter Finset Set
open scoped Topology

namespace Erdos1072

/-- For any prime $p$, let $f(p)$ be the least integer such that $f(p)! + 1 \equiv 0 \mod p$. -/
noncomputable def f (p : ℕ) : ℕ := sInf {n | (n)! + 1 ≡ 0 [MOD p]}

/-- Is it true that there are infinitely many $p$ for which $f(p) = p − 1$? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1072.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔ Set.Infinite {p | p.Prime ∧ f p = p - 1} := by
  sorry

/-- Is it true that $f(p)/p \to 0$ for $p \to \infty$ in a density 1 subset of the primes? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1072.parts.ii :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (P : Set ℕ), P ⊆ {p | p.Prime} ∧ P.HasDensity 1 {p | p.Prime} ∧
      Tendsto (fun p => (f p / p : ℝ)) (atTop ⊓ principal P) (𝓝 0) := by
  sorry
/--
Erdős, Hardy, and Subbarao [HaSu02], believed that the number of $p \le x$ for which $f(p)=p−1$
is $o(x/\log x)$.

[HaSu02] Hardy, G. E. and Subbarao, M. V., _A modified problem of Pillai and some related questions._
Amer. Math. Monthly (2002), 554--559.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1072.variants.littleo :
    (fun x ↦ (({p | p.Prime ∧ f p = p - 1} ∩ Icc 0 x).ncard : ℝ)) =o[atTop]
      (fun x ↦ x / Real.log x) := by
  sorry

end Erdos1072

reformulations.difference: The source says f(p)/p tends to zero 'for almost all p'; Lean explicitly chooses one relative-density-one subset of the primes and takes the limit along that subset.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: This is the standard density-one interpretation. It is also equivalent to statistical convergence: for every ε>0, the primes with f(p)/p≥ε have relative density zero. A density-one convergence set implies this immediately. Conversely, let E_k be the nested exceptional sets for ε=1/k. Choose increasing N_k so that E_k has relative proportion at most 1/k beyond N_k, and delete E_k on each block [N_k,N_{k+1}). The deleted set has relative density zero, and convergence holds on its complement. The density and ε–N expansions of the Lean statement were proved in the scratch file; the statistical-convergence diagonal argument was not formalized.

reformulations.difference: The cutoff x is a natural number in Lean, rather than an unrestricted real cutoff as commonly used for counting-function asymptotics.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For real x≥0, the number of qualifying primes ≤x equals the count at ⌊x⌋. Moreover, ⌊x⌋/log(⌊x⌋) is asymptotic to x/log x. Thus the natural-cutoff little-o statement implies the real-cutoff statement; restriction to natural cutoffs gives the converse. The full equivalence was proved as Review1072.littleo_cutoff_iff.

review.notes: All four declarations were checked against the cited website's exact LaTeX. Wilson's theorem was used in Lean to verify that f is a genuine minimum for every prime. Boundary checks include f(0)=f(1)=f(2)=0, f(3)=2, f(5)=4, and f(7)=3. Both quotients use real division; all counted sets are finite. Relative density one among primes was proved to force an infinite set and a non-bottom restricted filter. The combined experiments in /workspace/review/scratch.lean compile without errors, and the checked helper proofs do not depend on sorryAx. The source still records the problem as open. Full-text access to Hardy–Subbarao and Guy A2 was unavailable, so their original wording was not independently checked beyond the cited website.
